record.provider: git-annex rclone special remote (built into annex since 2023)

free_tier.stated: N/A. Front-end to rclone storage backends, inheriting free tiers of supported providers. Documentation lists Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega, pCloud, Box, Yandex, Jottacloud, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, Swift, B2, and S3.

egress.terms: Determined by the selected rclone backend. Rclone handles throttling and retries across remote endpoints.

record.tooling: Two paths: (a) `git annex initremote type=rclone ..`. Native, no extra install, documented via `rclone gitannex -h`; (b) the older `git-annex-remote-rclone` bash script (DanielDent, ~300 lines). rclone itself is a single static binary.
record.chaining: Combines git-annex versioning, checksum verification, and partial checkouts with rclone remote storage backends. A single repository can configure multiple rclone remotes across diverse storage providers using git annex copy commands.
record.limits_note: Per-backend: file size caps, per-day upload quotas, API rate limits all apply unchanged. rclone's Drive backend has its own 750 GB/day upload cap; OneDrive throttles. Encrypted annex remotes lose rclone's server-side dedupe.
record.reliability_note: Solid; the native remote removed the bash-script dependency. The failure mode is per-backend token expiry and drive-level rate limiting, which rclone surfaces as retries rather than data loss.

evidence.proved: 'With a recent version of rclone and git-annex, it is not necessary to install anything else, just use `git-annex initremote type=rclone ...`'
the gitannex bridge command exists in rclone proper

free_tier.stated: N/A by itself. Inherits whatever S3-compatible store you point it at. This is the multiplier: any free S3 endpoint (Internet Archive s3.us.archive.org, HF s3.hf.co, Oracle/Cloudflare-adjacent object tiers, MinIO on a free VM) becomes a versioned large-file store with git-annex's own manifest.

egress.terms: Determined by the backing S3 store. Parameter publicurl enables downloads via direct HTTP GET, and parameter signature=anonymous allows unauthenticated read-only access.

record.tooling: git-annex (Haskell, standalone Linux/macOS builds, ~1.5k stars on the mirror). Config via `git annex initremote type=S3 host=... bucket=... requeststyle=path`. Internet Archive has a documented special mode (`host=s3.us.archive.org`) where git-annex writes x-archive-meta-* headers and records the public URL, so every annexed file is also fetchable from archive.org with no login.
record.chaining: One special remote per bucket; `fileprefix=` lets many remotes share one bucket. The allowance is per account, so each free S3 account adds one bucket. Because git-annex keys content by hash, the S3 side is a dumb blob store. A client can shard the same dataset across several free stores, and git-annex tracks which copy is where (`git annex whereis`). Chunking (`chunk=1MiB`) avoids per-object size caps on the backing store.
record.limits_note: Depends on backend. Practical: `partsize=1GiB` needed for multipart; parts under 100 MiB are rejected by S3; `versioning=yes` means git-annex cannot drop content. No delete-resume; interrupted uploads restart. For IA specifically, uploads to the test collection vanish after 30 days and public visibility lags.
record.reliability_note: Mature and boring — the special remote has existed for over a decade. Failure mode is backend-side (IA's S3 endpoint was unreachable: connect timeout on s3.us.archive.org:443, and archive.org/help/abouts3.txt returned 522 through the proxy), not annex-side.

evidence.proved: 'git annex initremote archive type=S3 protocol=https host=s3.us.archive.org bucket=...' with x-archive-meta headers
built-in list: S3, rclone, webdav, rsync, directory, bup, ddar, git-lfs, httpalso, gcrypt

record.provider: git-annex git-lfs special remote (annex over any LFS host)

free_tier.stated: N/A. A protocol adapter. Turns ANY git-lfs server (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, a self-hosted Gitea) into an annex special remote, so the LFS host's quota applies but annex adds hash-verified partial clone and `whereis` across mirrors.

retention.stated: | Cannot delete = every mistake is permanent on the LFS side, and the host's month-storage accounting (GitHub) means you keep paying for it in quota

egress.terms: Determined by the underlying Git LFS host.

record.tooling: `git annex initremote lfstest type=git-lfs url=... encryption=shared`. Supports gcrypt:: URL prefix for encrypting the git side too.
record.chaining: Because annex can hold the same content on several LFS remotes, you can stack the 10 GiB/project GitLab allowance and the 10 GiB GitHub allowance as tiers of one logical dataset, with annex tracking which objects live where. Sharding a 1 TiB corpus across 100 GitLab projects becomes a `git annex copy --to` loop.
record.limits_note: Hard, documented limitations: 'The git-lfs protocol does not support deleting content, so git-annex cannot delete anything from a git-lfs special remote'; no upload resume; 'git-annex doesn't do batching. This may cause it to fall afoul of rate limiting of git-lfs servers' — which directly collides with GitLab's 1000 req/min LFS limit. Requires SHA256 backend for efficiency.
record.reliability_note: Cannot delete = every mistake is permanent on the LFS side, and the host's month-storage accounting (GitHub) means you keep paying for it in quota. No batching + per-object request = the exact workload LFS rate limits are designed to stop.

evidence.proved: example: 'git annex initremote lfstest type=git-lfs url=gcrypt::[address removed]:username/somerepo.git encryption=shared'

record.notes: N/A. A protocol adapter. Turns ANY git-lfs server (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, a self-hosted Gitea) into an annex special remote, so the LFS host's quota applies but annex adds hash-verified partial clone and `whereis` across mirrors.
